title: Damage Profile and Estimate Type: Acceptance Rules for Repair Estimates & Appointments
content:
**1. General rule.** The Repair Estimates & Appointments estimate type must accept the vehicle's damage profile. The damage profile recorded on the booking (structural damage, drivability, airbag deployment, high-voltage damage) is one the requested estimate type accepts.

**2. Condition by condition.** An estimate type accepts:

| Reported condition | Accepted only where the estimate type… |
|---|---|
| Structural damage | accepts structural damage |
| Vehicle cannot be driven | accepts a non-drivable vehicle |
| An airbag deployed | accepts a deployed airbag |
| Damage near a high-voltage system | accepts high-voltage damage |

**3. Choice of type.** When several estimate types accept the profile the customer chooses, and when none of the lower types do, the lowest type that accepts every reported condition is offered.

**4. Mobile Estimate.** A Mobile Estimate additionally requires the vehicle to be within the mobile service radius of the assigned center, measured as the service distance recorded on the booking.

**5. Insurer claim number.** For an insurance-claim booking on an estimate type that requires the insurer claim number at booking, the insurer claim number is recorded on the booking at booking time; without it that type cannot be booked and a lower type that accepts the damage profile is offered instead. The claim number is tied to the insurer's account profile on the booking.

**6. Source of the profile.** The damage profile is what the caller reports; it is corrected by the estimator on the written estimate and never re-checked against the estimate type after check-in.

### Points of judgement (hypothetical callers)

- A caller reports a drivable vehicle with no structural damage, no deployed airbag and no high-voltage damage: every type that accepts that profile is available and the customer chooses among them.
- A caller reports a deployed airbag: no type below the Blueprint Teardown Estimate accepts it, so the lowest type accepting every reported condition is offered.
- An insurer books a Structural Blueprint Estimate on a claim but has no claim number yet: that type cannot be booked; a lower type that accepts the damage profile is offered instead.
- After check-in the estimator finds structural damage the caller did not report: the profile is corrected on the written estimate; the booking is not re-checked against its type at that point.
